Shield(검증 레이어)는 4단계로 동작 — Tier 0: YAML 정책 룰(결정적), Tier 1: 휴리스틱 엔진 + DeBERTa 분류기(병렬), Tier 2: 별도 LLM 평가(예산 제한), Tier 3: 사람 승인. 모든 단계는 fail-closed(실패 시 차단).
Information Flow Control(IFC): Agent가 자격증명 파일을 읽으면 RESTRICTED 태그가 붙고, 이후 해당 데이터를 네트워크로 전송하려 할 때 Shield가 중간 단계가 몇 개이든 관계없이 차단 — 다단계 툴체인 공격 방어.
Dynamic Tool Surface Reduction: Agent는 매 턴마다 필요한 툴 그룹만 로드하고 나머지는 보이지 않아, 해킹당한 순간 사용 가능한 무기 자체가 최소화된다. 텍스트 분석 작업 중엔 툴 0개 = 공격 표면 0.
howToApply: Agent 서버를 2개의 OS 프로세스로 분리하라 — LLM 추론 프로세스는 gRPC 외 모든 권한을 제거하고, 툴 실행은 별도 Engine 프로세스에서만 수행. 기존 단일 프로세스 Agent 아키텍처라면 OpenParallax(Go) 소스코드를 참고해 프로세스 경계부터 재설계.
툴 등록 방식을 변경하라 — 모든 툴을 시스템 프롬프트에 한 번에 노출하지 말고, `load_tools` 메타툴 하나만 제공한 뒤 현재 태스크에 필요한 그룹만 동적 로드. 코딩 어시스턴트라면 파일 R/W 그룹과 쉘 실행 그룹을 별도로 두고 필요 시에만 활성화.
파괴적 액션(파일 삭제, DB 쓰기, 설정 변경) 전에는 반드시 Chronicle 패턴을 적용하라 — 액션 실행 전 SHA-256 기반 스냅샷을 저장하고 `rollback` 커맨드로 복구 가능하게. 기존 파이프라인에서 destructive action 분류만 추가해도 부분 적용 가능.

en.oneLinerEn: OS-level process isolation prevents prompt guardrail bypasses from compromised agents.
en.targetAudienceEn: Backend/platform developers building AI Agents that utilize real-world tools like file system access, shell execution, and API calls, as well as AI infrastructure engineers grappling with prompt injection defense strategies.
keyFindingsEn: Fundamental limitations of prompt guardrails: Safety instructions and malicious inputs share the same LLM attention mechanism, rendering prompt-level protection useless once an agent is compromised.

Parallax is an architectural paradigm comprised of four principles — (1) Cognitive-Executive Separation, (2) Adversarial Validation with Graduated Determinism, (3) Information Flow Control, and (4) Reversible Execution.
Cognitive-Executive Separation: The LLM inference process is sandboxed at the OS level, lacking any file system, network, or shell execution permissions, and can only propose actions via gRPC.

Shield (the validation layer) operates in four tiers — Tier 0: YAML policy rules (deterministic), Tier 1: Heuristic engine + DeBERTa classifier (parallel), Tier 2: Separate LLM evaluation (budget constrained), Tier 3: Human approval. All tiers are fail-closed.

Information Flow Control (IFC): If an agent reads a credentials file, it’s tagged RESTRICTED, and Shield blocks any subsequent attempt to transmit that data over the network, regardless of the number of intermediate stages — defending against multi-stage toolchain attacks.

Dynamic Tool Surface Reduction: Agents load only the necessary tool groups each turn, minimizing the attack surface should compromise occur. Zero tools loaded during text analysis = zero attack surface.
evidenceEn: 98.9% attack blockage and 0% false positives were achieved across 280 adversarial test cases (9 attack categories) with baseline settings. 100% blockage (36% false positives) was achieved with maximum security settings.
Assume-Compromise Evaluation (bypassing the inference system and directly injecting tool calls) showed a reduction in success rate from 100% in Config A (no Shield) to 1.1% in Config C (Parallax).

Shield tier processing distribution: Tier 0 (policy rules) 15.4%, Tier 1 (classifier) 58.2%, Tier 2 (LLM) 26.1%, Tier 3 (human) 0.4% — Deterministic mechanisms (Tier 0+1) handle 73.6% of requests, minimizing LLM reliance.

Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Haiku 4.5, and Llama 3.1 8B showed 0% attack success rate in LLM mode due to safety training, while Qwen 2.5 3B immediately executed harmful requests like file deletion — demonstrating the realistic potential for 'hacked agent' scenarios.
howToApplyEn: Separate the agent server into two OS processes — remove all permissions from the LLM inference process except gRPC, and perform tool execution only in a separate Engine process. If you have an existing single-process agent architecture, redesign it from the process boundary using the OpenParallax (Go) source code as a reference.

Change the tool registration method — do not expose all tools in the system prompt at once, but provide only one `load_tools` metatool and dynamically load only the groups needed for the current task. For coding assistants, keep file R/W groups and shell execution groups separate and activate them only when necessary.

Apply the Chronicle pattern before destructive actions (file deletion, DB writes, configuration changes) — save a SHA-256 based snapshot before action execution and enable recovery with a `rollback` command. Adding destructive action classification to an existing pipeline allows for partial application.
